counterfactual_missing_items: Family history was negative for similar findings
No evidence of Haab striae, buphthalmos, or high iris insertion
decisive_items: 2 heterozygous variants in the LTBP2 gene (c.709C>T p.Arg237* and c.3776-1G>C splice acceptor)
response.rationale: The presence of LTBP2 gene variants and the patient's symptoms of elevated intraocular pressure, lens dislocation, and joint hypermobility are most consistent with Weill-Marchesani syndrome due to LTBP2 gene variants.

rejected.why: The absence of characteristic anterior segment findings and the atypical age of onset make pseudoexfoliation syndrome less likely.
The lack of family history, absence of cardiac involvement, and other characteristic findings make Marfan syndrome less likely.
The absence of other typical findings such as skin hyperextensibility makes Ehlers-Danlos syndrome less likely.
